info.title: CleanNest enquiry API
info.description: Accepts a cleaning enquiry for CleanNest, a cleaning company based in Jalandhar, Punjab, and delivers it to the business. This is the site's only interface intended to be called by visitors. It is public but gated by a Cloudflare Turnstile token, so it is meant to be called from the cleannest.in pages rather than by unattended agents, which cannot obtain a token. The site also exposes a WhatsApp webhook at /api/whatsapp, but that is Meta's callback rather than a visitor interface: it is documented here only so this description is complete, and it rejects every request that is not signed by Meta.

post.description: Validates the enquiry and sends it to the business. Values are trimmed and clamped to the documented maximum lengths; control characters are stripped. On success the enquiry has been delivered, and there is no idempotency key — a repeated identical request is a second enquiry.

400.description: `invalid_json` for a malformed or non-object body, `name_required` when name is empty, `phone_invalid` when the phone number is not 10-15 digits after non-digits are stripped.

403.description: `captcha_failed` — the Turnstile token was missing, rejected, or could not be verified.

502.description: `send_failed` — the enquiry passed validation but could not be delivered downstream.

503.description: `not_configured` — captcha verification or delivery is not configured in this deployment.

get.summary: Meta webhook verification (not a visitor interface)
get.description: The one-time handshake Meta performs when the webhook URL is saved in the WhatsApp Business app configuration. Echoes `hub.challenge` back as plain text when `hub.verify_token` matches the deployment's configured token, and returns 403 otherwise — including when no token is configured, so an unconfigured deployment refuses subscriptions rather than accepting them.

403.description: The mode is not `subscribe`, the token does not match, or no verify token is configured.

post.summary: Inbound WhatsApp message delivery (called by Meta, not by clients)
post.description: Receives message deliveries from the WhatsApp Business Cloud API. Every request must carry a valid `X-Hub-Signature-256` HMAC of the raw body computed with the app secret; an unsigned or mis-signed body is rejected with 401 and never reaches the send path. The first message from a given number within a 24-hour window is answered once with a greeting, and repeat messages in that window are ignored. Messages the business sends from the WhatsApp Business app are echoed back by Meta under a separate field and are never answered. The response is 200 even when an outbound reply fails, because Meta retries any other status and a retry would greet the customer twice.

200.description: The delivery was accepted and processed. `greeted` counts the greetings actually sent.

400.description: `invalid_json` — the signed body was not valid JSON.

401.description: `bad_signature` — the `X-Hub-Signature-256` header was missing or did not match the app secret.

405.description: `method_not_allowed` — this path accepts only GET (verification) and POST (delivery).

503.description: `not_configured` — no app secret is set in this deployment, so no delivery can be authenticated.

phone.description: Contact number. Non-digits are stripped, so spacing and punctuation are accepted. A 10-digit number is treated as Indian and prefixed with 91; 10 to 15 digits are required, and the digits are what is delivered.

when.description: Free-text preferred timing, passed through to the business unchanged.

notes.description: Free-text notes. Line breaks are preserved.

services.description: The services the enquiry is about. At most 20 are kept; each is clamped to 80 characters and any that are empty after trimming are dropped.

turnstileToken.description: Cloudflare Turnstile response token. Required — the endpoint rejects the request without a verifiable token.
